subject: P0 E2 CYCLE-1 FINDING: Beta2 wake retry weakens execution-time generation/connection fencing
body: Current-head Beta2 patcher audit found a concrete transaction-boundary regression in transformed Fold7ContinuityCoordinator.wakeInner. Baseline coordinator checks controller.isGenerationCurrent(generation) both before queueing and again inside the IO coroutine immediately before ShizukuBridge.wakeInnerDisplay(). Beta2 replacement instead admits a stale generation whenever controller.state is OPENING_FROM_CLOSED/INNER_HANDOFF, then queues IO without a second generation check immediately before the privileged call. It also does not capture/revalidate Shizuku connectionEpoch around the call. After completion, the handler can treat current topology as proof and, when not ready, schedules the next retry with generation=controller.generation rather than the original request generation. Therefore a queued request can execute after generation/connection supersession, and an old attempt result can seed a retry in a new generation. Shell WAKE_INNER_DISPLAY carries no generation/attempt token; shell-side wake mutates physical NORMAL then may enable/power a matched 1968x2184 logical route. This is SOURCE evidence, not yet a physical crash/wake causal claim. E2 cycle 2 will model adversarial interleavings and propose fail-closed call-boundary semantics without duplicating broad regression-gate ownership.

finding.beta2: stale generation admitted while opening; no immediate pre-invocation generation or connectionEpoch fence
finding.postcall: retry uses controller.generation, allowing lineage hop
